sentences: Toda's theorem in discrete complexity relates alternating quantifiers to counting power.
This source asks for an analogous relationship among real-algebraic complexity classes.
The proposed target is to contain fixed levels of alternating real quantification in an existential real theory enhanced with summation operators.
The exact operator language matters because unrestricted real exponentiation would change the setting substantially.
A positive result would organize several real-feasibility hierarchies under one strengthened existential framework and illuminate the role of counting-like operations over real computation.
